newsitem.title: UK: ZENECA SEES SUBSTANTIAL LAUNCH COSTS IN H2.
newsitem.headline: ZENECA SEES SUBSTANTIAL LAUNCH COSTS IN H2.

text.p: British drugs and chemicals company Zeneca Group Plc said on Thursday it faced "substantial" costs in the second half of the year as it moves to launch a raft of new products, including asthma treatment Accolate in Europe and migraine drug Zomig.
In a telephone interview with Reuters, chief executive Sir David Barnes said "there will be substantial new product launch costs in the second half of the year."

Barnes said profit margins, which rose strongly to 24.0 percent of sales in the first half of the year from 21.2 percent a year earlier, were likely to be between two and 2.5 percentage points lower for the full year, taking into account most of the launch costs.

The drop in full-year margins is in line with Zeneca's historic performance, which is affected by the seasonal nature of its agrochemical business, which is heavily-weighted towards the first half of the year.

Barnes said among products likely to be launched later this year were Accolate in Europe, Zomig "hopefully in the U.S," and schizophrenia drug Seroquel, which has won approval in Britain and been granted approvable status in the U.S.
